Fir Cup is a fictional cafe selling coffee and pre-ordered pastry boxes. Its public website is fixture://fir-cup/about. The owner uses Google Drive for menus and Gmail for customer inquiries; these are fictional tool examples, not connected accounts.
tone
Brand writing is friendly, brief and plain. Avoid hype and guarantees. An owner-written example is: Thanks for thinking of us. Tell us your pickup time and we will check what is available.
policy

The fictional owner currently requires 24 hours of notice for pastry-box orders. Pickup availability must be checked by a staff member. Discounts require a separate owner decision; no automatic discount has been approved.
workflow

Staff read a customer request, check availability, then prepare a reply for review. Gmail is the inquiry channel. There is no separate booking platform. A past successful order is not evidence of current availability.
customer

ai-suggestion

Sample Film is a fictional flexible-packaging factory making custom PE bags. It has no website or SNS. The owner supplied this company introduction and uses spreadsheet files for specifications and Gmail for inquiries. This is not Hanafilm or any real owner business.
tone
Customer writing is practical, precise and courteous. Ask for missing dimensions and material thickness. Do not claim certification or food suitability without evidence.
policy

The fictional owner currently requires a 25% deposit before a custom production order is accepted. Quotes require bag dimensions, film thickness, print requirements and quantity. Delivery dates need production review.
workflow
Sales collect specifications, production checks feasibility, the owner approves the quote, then the deposit is requested. Spreadsheets hold order records. There is no POS or booking system.
customer
A fictional buyer asks for 10,000 printed bags by Friday but has supplied neither dimensions nor thickness. The request does not establish capacity or a delivery promise.
ai-suggestion
